newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi says beheading effective against drug trade.
newsitem.headline: Saudi says beheading effective against drug trade.

text.p: Saudi Arabia said its policy of beheading drug smugglers was proving effective in fighting the trade and hoped other Arab and Islamic countries would impose the death penalty on traffickers.

"The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia urged the world's countries to collectively work to fight the killer drug problem and expressed its hope that Arab and Islamic countries work to implement the punishment of execution against drug smugglers and pushers," the official Saudi Press Agency (SPA) said late on Saturday.
Its comments were made in a report on an Arab conference on combating drug trafficking in the Arab world.

Saudi Deputy Interior Minister Prince Ahmed bin Abdul-Aziz told the conference in Jeddah that Saudi Arabia considers its implementation of Islamic sharia law by publicly beheading convicted murderers, rapists and drug smugglers, "a salvation of humanity from the crime in all its shapes."

"This decisive policy of punishment contributes to deterring those with weak spirits who are after material gains at the expense of the security and safety of our societies," SPA quoted him as saying.
He said the implementation of the death penalty for drug smugglers was instrumental in the fight against drugs coming into the kingdom.

SPA said an Arab study discussed at the conference put the amounts of hashish confiscated in the Arab world between 1994 and 1996 at 208,000 kg (460,000 lb), opium 80 kg (175 lb), heroin 2,586 kg (5,700 lb), cocaine 470 kg (1,035 lb). It said 163,000 drug smugglers were arrested in the same period, including 8,000 non-Arabs.
Saudi Arabia has so far this year beheaded 54 people, including 18 for drug smuggling -- most of them Pakistanis.
Several other Arab and Islamic countries impose the death penalty for drugs smuggling.
